current.text: Claxton was traded from Brooklyn to the Bulls.
He is on a two-year deal with Chicago.
He is projected to start at center for the Bulls. One expert puts it at about 90% that he starts over Jalen Smith.
He hurt his hamstring on 2026-10-05. Yahoo lists him as questionable with a hamstring injury.
Because of the hamstring injury, one expert would move him down the draft board.
He may not reach 30 minutes if the Bulls rotate their centers and use Jalen Smith for spacing or Zach Collins.
Experts call him fair value around rank 100 to 120 but too expensive in the 80s.
In an auction, Josh would pay no more than about 3 USD for him.
Josh has low hopes for him because he has looked disinterested and has struggled.
The Bulls are projected to be a bad team. One expert predicts 32 wins and another calls them a bottom-10 team.
Tiago Splitter is the new Bulls head coach. Nikola Vucevic is gone, which leaves the starting center job to Claxton.
The Bulls should play a fast, up-tempo transition style.
The Bulls have 15 back-to-backs, one below the maximum. They play 10 games in our fantasy playoff weeks (3-3-4).
The Bulls front office signs veterans to short deals and hopes to trade them, so trades are possible this season.

durable.text: His blocks and rim protection have fallen for three straight seasons.
His play has dropped off over the last two to three seasons. Experts suggest back problems, decline or frustration in Brooklyn as reasons, and are not sure whether he is washed.
He is a very poor free throw shooter, and his FT% clearly hurts a team.
He fits a switching, blitzing defensive scheme. Brooklyn had pushed him out to the perimeter.
He is slightly better in points leagues than in category leagues.

note: He is a late-auction center. Yahoo values him at 3 USD, ESPN at 1 USD, and he went for 4 USD in our league last season. His Yahoo rank of 110 and ESPN rank of 121 fall in the range experts call fair (100 to 120), so do not pay more than about 3 to 4 USD. He fits punt FT% builds best: his projected FG% (59%) and blocks (1.3) help, while his FT% and threes hurt. Early in the season, check whether the hamstring injury costs games, whether he holds the starting job and close to 30 minutes ahead of Jalen Smith and Zach Collins, and whether his blocks recover in Chicago.
